countersubjects.first: present in exposition (begins before this part)

claims.claim: At bar 6 the alto develops the semiquavers of bar 5 into a second countersubject; thereafter variants of the semiquaver run count as that countersubject
After episode 1 (10-13) there is a counterexposition, with chromatic alteration of the subject at bar 14
All four voices sound together for the first time in the climactic passage 22-24
Bar 24 is the 'original final cadence', adorned by a suspended seventh; modulation begins immediately with the alto in vi
Episode 2 modulates from iii to v; tenor enters with the subject in v at 32
Bass entry at 37 has its accents reversed, a latent possibility of this subject; it begins in IV and ends in iv
At 41-43 the bass answer arrives before the tenor subject has finished, and is harmonized toward the Neapolitan (bII) instead of V
The coda from bar 46 adds a fifth part and includes a final subject entry starting like the answer, with the first countersubject
Episode 2 (27-32) is a complete interchange and extension of episode 1
